name: St. JOHN Smithfield
description: Fergus Henderson's nose-to-tail British restaurant (1994), beside Smithfield Market — the birthplace of modern British cooking. Bone marrow and parsley salad is legendary.
tips: Book weeks ahead for dinner. Lunch is easier. Don't skip the Eccles cake with Lancashire cheese.

name: Rochelle Canteen
description: Margot Henderson's understated lunch-only canteen inside a converted Victorian schoolhouse bike shed — the Shoreditch insiders' secret.
tips: Ring the bell to enter — the door is unmarked. Book ahead; menu changes daily.

name: The Clove Club
description: Shoreditch Town Hall's Michelin-starred tasting-menu restaurant with strong British ingredients and Japanese technique.
tips: Tasting menu only. Book 2 months ahead.

name: Brat
description: Basque-style open-fire cooking in Shoreditch — the whole-roasted turbot is unforgettable. Michelin-starred.
address: First Floor, 4 Redchurch St, London E1 6JL
tips: Sister restaurant Brat Climpson's Arch on weekends only.

name: Lyle's
description: James Lowe's modern-British fine-dining canteen in Shoreditch — the antithesis of showy, with immaculate seasonal plates.
address: Tea Building, 56 Shoreditch High St, London E1 6JJ
tips: Lunch tasting menu is a relative bargain at £45.

name: Noble Rot Bloomsbury
description: The original of London's best wine-focused restaurants — a smart dining room with a wine list that reads like a collection.
tips: Two sister restaurants now — Soho and Mayfair. Stick with the original.

name: Noble Rot Soho
description: The second Noble Rot, in the former Gay Hussar site on Greek Street — bigger, buzzier, same serious wine list.
tips: Downstairs is quieter; upstairs has the buzz.

name: Andrew Edmunds
description: A dimly-lit Georgian-era Soho townhouse favourite since 1985 — British-European food, a cult following, tiny tables close together.
tips: The wine list is legendary. Book weeks ahead.

name: Barrafina Dean Street
description: Stand-at-the-counter Spanish tapas, a step-in-Seville experience in Soho. No reservations; bloody brilliant.
tips: Arrive at opening (12 or 5) to grab a seat. Three branches — Covent Garden and Adelaide Street are the others.

name: Bocca di Lupo
description: Regional Italian cooking in Soho — small plates let you travel the Italian regions. Gelateria Ventini, its sister ice cream parlour, is directly opposite.
tips: Counter seats are best — watch the kitchen.

name: Yauatcha Soho
description: Michelin-starred all-day dim sum in a jade-lit Soho space — the venison puffs and cheung fun alone are worth the trip.
tips: Don't miss the patisserie downstairs — jewel-like cakes to take away.

name: Koya Soho
description: A tiny Japanese udon counter on Frith Street — hand-made noodles, quicksilver service, late-lunch perfection.
tips: No reservations for lunch. Walk-ins only; expect a short wait.

name: Kiln
description: Thai charcoal-grill counter cooking in a tiny Brewer Street space — smoke, spice, and sublime noodles. Bar seating only.
tips: Can't book upstairs — walk in and queue. Downstairs takes bookings.

name: Smoking Goat Shoreditch
description: Spicy, smoky Thai food in Shoreditch — crab ssam and fish-sauce wings are the house classics.
tips: Bring extra tissues — chilli-heat is authentic.

name: Som Saa
description: A former-pop-up now permanent Thai restaurant in Spitalfields — regional northern and Isan cooking, family-run with industrial-chic decor.
tips: The deep-fried sea bass with three-flavour sauce is a signature dish.

name: Singburi Royal Thai Café
description: A cult Leytonstone Thai — home-style Bangkok cooking, BYOB, served by a husband-and-wife team since 2002.
tips: BYOB. Book weeks ahead for weekend nights.

name: Mangal Ocakbasi
description: Dalston's original Turkish charcoal-grill restaurant (1994) — smoky lamb kofta, adana, and whole sea bream over coals.
tips: BYO wine (small corkage). The artist Gilbert & George are fixtures.

name: Mangal 2
description: The second Mangal next door — fuller menu including mezze and lahmacun, slightly more refined. Same family, also beloved.
tips: Book for weekends.

name: Moro
description: The Clerkenwell restaurant that invented Moorish-Mediterranean cooking for London — beloved of broadsheet critics since 1997.
tips: Sister Morito next door is smaller and tapas-focused.

name: Morito
description: Moro's little-sister tapas bar on Exmouth Market — smaller plates, walk-in friendly, as good as the mothership.
tips: Walk-ins preferred; small plates pass quickly.

name: The Quality Chop House
description: A 1869 working-class Farringdon chop house, Grade-II listed — now a restaurant serving seasonal British food in the original wooden booths.
tips: The Quality Wines wine-shop next door serves £14 lunches at the counter.

name: Lahore Kebab House
description: Whitechapel's legendary Punjabi institution (1974) — mixed grills, karahi meat, naan straight from the tandoor. BYOB.
tips: BYOB. No booking; arrive before 7pm weekends.

name: Tayyabs
description: Punjabi restaurant in Whitechapel since 1972 — famed for lamb chops and seekh kebabs. BYOB, queues, chaos, excellent food.
tips: BYOB. Off-licence across the road. Book ahead — walk-in queues can be 1h+.

name: Needoo Grill
description: A former Tayyabs head chef's own Whitechapel grill — same cooking, smaller queues, similar BYOB vibes.
tips: BYOB. Walk-in friendly.

name: Bundobust Mayfair
description: Gujarati vegetarian small-plates restaurant paired with a vast craft-beer menu — an unlikely match that works brilliantly.
tips: All-vegetarian. Okra fries and vada pav are essential.

name: Gymkhana
description: Karam Sethi's Mayfair Indian, modelled on Raj-era colonial club — two Michelin stars for regional Indian dining in a clubby setting.
tips: Book months ahead. Lunch set menu £50.

name: Trishna
description: The Karam Sethi-family's original — Mumbai-style coastal seafood in Marylebone. Michelin-starred and unflashy.
tips: Prawn koliwada and Guinea-fowl pepper fry are signatures.

name: Brigadiers
description: Sethi family's Indian military-mess-themed beer-hall in Bloomberg Arcade — tandoori, grills, craft beers and a great TV sports scene.
tips: Live sport on multiple screens. Cricket fanatics gather here.

name: Kricket Soho
description: Small-plates modern Indian cooking with bar counter seating — a runaway hit since opening 2017. Three branches now.
tips: Bookable but bar seats walk-in only.

name: Dishoom Covent Garden
description: The flagship of the beloved Bombay-cafe chain, occupying three floors including the Permit Room cocktail bar.
address: 12 Upper St Martin's Ln, London WC2H 9FB
tips: Breakfast (until 11:30am) is always walk-in. Bacon Naan the star.

name: Dishoom King's Cross
description: A 1920s industrial warehouse repurposed as the biggest Dishoom — with a vast railway-and-warehouse-themed dining room.
tips: Most bookable Dishoom. The Permit Room cocktail bar upstairs is excellent.

name: Dishoom Kensington
description: West London Dishoom occupying a gorgeous Art Deco listed building — with a separate Colaba-bar members' lounge.
tips: Breakfast always walk-in; dinners bookable 14 days ahead.

name: Dishoom Canary Wharf
description: Canary Wharf's Dishoom, in a converted dock building — expansive and airy, often the least-queued branch.
tips: Weekdays busy with office lunchers. Weekends far more relaxed.

name: Hoppers Soho
description: Sri Lankan café of coconut pancakes, curries and kottu — the Karam Sethi / JKS group's fresh Soho hit since 2015.
tips: Walk-ins only. Arrive before 6pm for dinner; expect a short wait.

name: Hoppers King's Cross
description: The larger Hoppers, opposite Central Saint Martins — same menu, takes bookings.
tips: Bookable. Try the black pork curry with an egg hopper.

name: BAO Soho
description: Taiwanese-style gua bao steamed buns in a stylishly minimal counter on Lexington Street — no reservations, queue-worthy.
tips: Walk-in queue. Classic pork bao is non-negotiable.

name: BAO Fitzrovia
description: Bigger sister of BAO Soho, with a full menu of Taiwanese specialties including guabao-burger and Chairman fry-up.
tips: Takes bookings. Ask for the downstairs karaoke rooms if in a group.

name: BAO King's Cross
description: The counter version of BAO for a quick quality lunch — perfectly thick pancakes filled to order.
tips: Pick-up-and-go. Perfect pre-Eurostar lunch.

name: XU
description: JKS Restaurants' Taipei teahouse in Soho — elegant tatami-room-style dining, minimalist, perfect for special occasions.
tips: Book upstairs for the best atmosphere. Chilli-oil dumplings are the signature.

name: Bar Shu
description: Soho's authentic Sichuan restaurant — genuinely spicy, Michelin-recognised, home to the city's best mapo tofu.
tips: Water-boiled fish is the spiciest dish in Soho. Proceed with caution.

name: Hunan
description: Pimlico's chef's-choice Hunanese restaurant since 1982 — no menu, just small courses until you tap out. Gordon Ramsay's favourite Chinese.
tips: About 15-18 courses. Dietary requests accepted but menu unfixed.

name: Min Jiang
description: 10th-floor Chinese restaurant at the Royal Garden Hotel — Beijing wood-fired duck and Kensington Gardens views.
tips: Order the duck 24 hours ahead for the best effect.

name: Hakkasan Mayfair
description: Michelin-starred glamorous Chinese in a candle-lit basement — the flagship of the Hakkasan group, a design icon.
tips: Dress smart. The dim sum lunch menu is more affordable.

name: Kiku
description: Traditional Japanese restaurant in Mayfair — a 40-year local institution with omakase sushi and private rooms.
tips: Omakase sushi at the counter is the move.

name: Sushi Atelier
description: A small Fitzrovia omakase sushi counter — 13 courses of nigiri and maki, with good-value lunch sittings.
tips: Lunch omakase £45; dinner from £100.

name: Roka Charlotte Street
description: The flagship of the Roka Japanese-robata group — a vast robatayaki grill as centrepiece, cocktails at downstairs Shochu Lounge.
tips: Lunch is more affordable. Shochu Lounge downstairs for cocktails after.

name: Zuma
description: Knightsbridge Japanese import from Rainer Becker — robatayaki, sushi, and sake in a buzzy, loud space.
tips: Sake flight pairing is the move. Book 2 weeks ahead.

name: Nobu Berkeley St
description: The high-wattage Mayfair branch of the Robert De Niro Japanese-Peruvian chain — black-cod with miso still worth the hype.
tips: Celebrity-friendly. The original Nobu on Park Lane is quieter.

name: Umu
description: Two Michelin-starred Kyoto-style kaiseki — the most authentic high-end Japanese in Mayfair, with a 180-sake list.
tips: Kaiseki tasting menu is the signature experience.

name: Dinings
description: Marylebone basement izakaya of bespoke sushi and micro-seasonal small plates — a long-standing critics' favourite.
tips: Sushi bar seats have a live-kitchen view.

name: Hawksmoor Seven Dials
description: The flagship of the British steakhouse chain — dry-aged longhorn beef in a former 1920s Covent Garden brewery.
tips: Express menu £30 for starter, main and side — Mon-Sat 5-6:30pm.

name: Hawksmoor Borough
description: The Borough Market outpost — vast glass-roofed Victorian room. Same legendary steaks, same Sunday roast.
address: Borough Market, 16 Winchester Walk, London SE1 9AQ
tips: Sunday roast is bookable; arrive hungry.

name: Goodman Mayfair
description: American-style dry-aged steakhouse in Mayfair — more New York than London in feel, with spectacular tomahawks.
tips: Four branches across London. Mayfair is the original.

name: Smith's of Smithfield
description: Rooftop-terrace steak-and-seafood restaurant above Smithfield Market — multiple floors of increasing formality, views of St Paul's from the top.
tips: Rooftop has a view, 2nd floor is more intimate.

name: Flat Iron Covent Garden
description: Single-cut flat-iron steaks at affordable prices — no reservations, consistently packed.
tips: Walk-in only. Eleven branches across London.

name: Blacklock Shoreditch
description: Chophouse-style British restaurant on Rivington Street — vintage charm, all-in Sunday roasts, Italian-style cocktails.
tips: All-in-chops lunch £18. Five branches now.

name: Blacklock Soho
description: The original Blacklock — a basement chophouse on Great Windmill Street, Britain's best £25 chop menu.
tips: Pre-theatre menu £25 — real value.

name: Chotto Matte
description: Soho's Nikkei (Peruvian-Japanese) restaurant — neon-graffiti interior, robata grill, and some of the best pisco sours in town.
tips: Booking essential weekends.

name: COYA Mayfair
description: Pisco bar and Peruvian cebicheria in Mayfair — a celebrity-frequented basement with ceviche counter and live DJs.
tips: COYA Pisco Lounge open later with DJs.

name: LIMA Fitzrovia
description: London's first Peruvian Michelin star holder — refined ceviche and anticuchos in a calm Fitzrovia room.
tips: Tasting menu £85. Lunch set £29.

name: Casa do Frango Bermondsey
description: Portuguese peri-peri chicken in a shed-like Bermondsey space — £14 half-chickens, cheap wines, constant queues.
tips: Walk-in friendly. Three branches — Shoreditch is flashier.

name: Casa do Frango Soho
description: The Heddon Street branch with a full menu of Algarve-style peri chicken, small plates, and custard tarts.
tips: Bookable. Pair with a Super Bock.

name: Casa Cruz
description: Mayfair's glamorous Argentine steakhouse imported from Buenos Aires — a beloved haunt of fashion-industry diners.
tips: Reservations booked months ahead.

name: Sabor
description: Michelin-starred regional Spanish — two floors: a counter-seat El Cafe downstairs, a dining room upstairs.
tips: Downstairs counter is where the action is.

name: José
description: Tiny Bermondsey tapas bar run by chef José Pizarro — stand-at-the-counter Spanish eating at its most genuine.
tips: Walk-in only. Pizarro restaurant next door takes bookings.

name: Pizarro
description: The fuller-menu sister of José — Bermondsey Street Spanish with full mains and bigger tables.
tips: Book ahead. The pan con tomate is a marvel.

name: Quo Vadis
description: Soho dining room and private members' club — Jeremy Lee's witty British-European cooking, glamorous dining room.
tips: The smoked eel sandwich is famous. Karl Marx once lived upstairs.

name: Duck & Rice
description: Chef Alan Yau's dim-sum-and-craft-beer pub concept on Berwick Street — a pub with the best har gow in Soho.
tips: Dim sum bar upstairs, pub downstairs. Walk-in-friendly downstairs.

name: Spring
description: Skye Gyngell's bright, botanical dining room inside Somerset House — garden-led cooking, extraordinary setting.
address: New Wing, Somerset House, London WC2R 1LA
tips: Scratch Menu (pre-theatre 5:30-6:45) uses the day's surplus.

name: Ottolenghi Islington
description: The original Ottolenghi deli — vegetables-first Middle Eastern counter eats with a stunning cake display.
tips: Four London branches; this was first. Take-away is as delicious.

name: NOPI
description: Yotam Ottolenghi's flagship restaurant — a bright airy Soho dining room of shared plates across Middle East and Southeast Asia.
tips: Brunch is a popular alternative to dinner.

name: Rovi
description: Ottolenghi's fire-and-fermentation restaurant on Wells Street — smoky vegetables, pickling, and a cult wine list.
tips: Natural wine list is remarkable.

name: Berber & Q Grill House
description: Smoky Middle Eastern barbecue in Haggerston — lamb shoulder roasted for 12 hours is essential.
tips: In a railway arch — atmospheric. Book ahead.

name: Shawarma Bar by Berber & Q
description: The Berber & Q takeaway/sit-in of nuclear-good shawarma wraps in Exmouth Market.
tips: Wraps from £10. Counter seats only.

name: The Palomar
description: Soho's modern Jerusalem cuisine — open counter and nightly singalongs, a buzzing 20-seat bar and room.
tips: Bar seats only take walk-ins. Booking for the back room.

name: The Barbary
description: Neal's Yard sister to The Palomar — North African cooking at a horseshoe counter; 24 seats around a central grill.
tips: Counter seats mean watching the grill fire. Walk-in first hour.

name: Gunpowder
description: Small-plates Indian in Spitalfields — tiny dining room, punchy home-style dishes, seriously good venison doughnuts.
tips: Walk-in: arrive at opening 5:30pm or queue.

name: Kolamba
description: Sri Lankan family cooking in Soho — dhal, devilled prawns, lamprais and hoppers in a warm, bright room.
tips: The 'Kolamba Classic' menu offers a full introduction.

name: Rambutan
description: Cynthia Shanmugalingam's modern Sri Lankan cooking at Borough Market — hot-pink booth seats, banana-leaf plates, ambitious flavours.
tips: Book ahead for dinner — tiny room.

name: Tandoor Chop House
description: British-Indian chop house on Adelaide Street — sigri grill, clay-oven cooking, and the only tandoori Sunday roast in town.
tips: Sunday roast is a tandoori chicken extravaganza.

name: Royal China Club Baker Street
description: High-end Cantonese dining in Marylebone — lavish private rooms and some of London's best dim sum.
tips: Dim sum served until 4pm; dinner after 5pm.

name: Kym's
description: Andrew Wong's City restaurant focused on Chinese roast meats — tea-smoked duck, crispy pork belly, soy-poached chicken.
tips: Three-bird roast for groups is a spectacle.

name: A. Wong
description: Andrew Wong's two-Michelin-starred Victoria restaurant — a Chinese regional tasting menu journey that is critically unrivalled.
tips: Book 2-3 months ahead. Dim sum lunch set £95.

name: The Ledbury
description: Brett Graham's Notting Hill restaurant — two Michelin stars, game-obsessive, back at top form since 2022 reopening.
tips: Tasting menu only. Book 3 months ahead.

name: Core by Clare Smyth
description: Three Michelin stars — Clare Smyth's elegant Notting Hill restaurant, Gordon Ramsay's former head chef at her best.
tips: Potato and roe dish is now legendary. Book 3 months ahead.

name: Le Manoir aux Quat'Saisons (day trip)
description: Raymond Blanc's two-Michelin-starred country-house restaurant in Oxfordshire — 40 minutes from Paddington, a destination meal.
tips: Lunch tasting menu £195. Taxi from Haddenham & Thame station.

name: Ikoyi
description: Michelin two-star restaurant at 180 The Strand — Jeremy Chan's spice-forward cooking that defies categorisation.
tips: Tasting menu only. Book as soon as you know the date.

name: Kiln — Brewer Street
description: Ben Chapman's open-kitchen Thai restaurant — counter-service, wood-fire, a thrilling dinner experience.
tips: Counter walk-in only. Downstairs bookable.

name: The Wolseley
description: Jeremy King's grand European brasserie on Piccadilly — the marble-floored breakfast of choice for London's power brokers.
tips: Breakfast 7-11:30am. Afternoon tea 2:30-5:30pm. Kedgeree for breakfast is classic.

name: The Delaunay
description: Jeremy King's Viennese-inspired café-restaurant near Aldwych — the elegant sister to The Wolseley.
tips: Viennese Konditorei counter for pastries, coffees, and cakes.

name: Colbert
description: A Parisian-style café-brasserie on Sloane Square — red leather banquettes, steak-frites, oeufs en cocotte, from Jeremy King & Chris Corbin.
tips: Early-evening set menu £25.

name: Fischer's
description: Jeremy King's Marylebone High Street Viennese grill — schnitzels, sachertorte, and imperial-era charm.
tips: Schnitzel Holstein is the signature.

name: Brasserie Zédel
description: Vast 1930s Parisian brasserie on Sherwood Street — £13 three-course prix-fixe and live cabaret in the attached Crazy Coqs.
tips: Remarkable-value menu. Crazy Coqs cabaret nightly from 9pm.

name: Bentley's Oyster Bar & Grill
description: Richard Corrigan's century-old Piccadilly oyster bar — marble counter, expert shuckers, Galway oysters flown in daily.
tips: Oyster bar downstairs; full-service grill upstairs.

name: Sweetings
description: The City's Victorian fish restaurant (1889), lunchtime-only, cash-preferred — potted shrimps and Dover sole for generations of City men.
tips: No bookings. Closed weekends and evenings. Arrive early.

name: Wiltons
description: Britain's oldest restaurant (1742) — oysters, grouse, a tradition-bound Mayfair dining room with a jacket-required policy.
tips: Jacket required. Royal Warrant holders — it feels it.

name: Rules
description: London's oldest restaurant (1798), Maiden Lane — Edwardian opulence, British game, Graham Greene's favourite.
tips: Cocktail bar upstairs is a lovely way to see the rooms without a full meal.

name: Simpson's in the Strand
description: 1828 grand-hotel carvery — trolleys of roast beef rolled to the table, an Empire-era dining institution.
tips: Carver's roast beef is the signature experience.

name: The Ritz Restaurant
description: Escoffier-era dining under rococo ceilings — the only hotel dining room with a Michelin star in the country, gold-leafed glory.
tips: Strict dress code — jacket required. Afternoon tea is the most accessible entry point.

name: Kensington Palace Pavilion
description: The Orangery at Kensington Palace reimagined as a garden-to-table bistro — airy, glass-walled, perfect for afternoon tea.
tips: Afternoon tea here is a calmer alternative to central hotels.

name: Skylon at the Royal Festival Hall
description: Three floors of dining-and-drinks with river views — all-day menu, cocktail bar, fine-dining restaurant, all under one glass wall.
tips: Bar has best view; restaurant has best food. Pre-theatre menu £35.

name: Oxo Tower Restaurant
description: Eighth-floor riverside modern European — panoramic Thames views from St Paul's to London Eye.
address: Oxo Tower Wharf, Barge House St, London SE1 9PH
tips: Terrace seating in summer. Brasserie below is cheaper with same view.

name: Sea Containers Restaurant & Bar
description: Riverside restaurant and rooftop terrace (Rumpus Room) — Thames views, all-day menu, classic London landmark from Frank Gehry's neighbour.
tips: Rumpus Room bar on roof for cocktails with river view.
